meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Taiwan (sub-state jurisdiction of the People's Republic of China; investor home jurisdiction for a PRC Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA), Cross-Strait, signed 2010 and effective 2010
Cross-Strait Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement, signed 2012 and effective 2013

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision); Counter-Terrorism Law of the People's Republic of China (2018 amendment); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Legal Entities (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective November 1, 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective January 1, 2020); Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act, as applicable to the Taiwanese investing entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Company Registration Certificate of the Taiwan investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company and Commercial Registration Office, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notarial certification then authentication by the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office (TECO) then Consular Legalization by the Embassy/Consulate of the People's Republic of China in the relevant jurisdiction. If the document is issued in a Hague Apostille Contracting State, the exclusive alternative path is notarization (if required) plus an Apostille certificate; the Apostille and Consular Legalization tracks are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Company Registration Record of the Taiwan investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notarial certification then TECO authentication then Consular Legalization by a PRC diplomatic mission for non-Apostille jurisdictions. For a Hague Apostille State, the sole acceptable path is notarization plus Apostille; no Consular Legalization may be added to an Apostille chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing formation of the PRC Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture and execution of all pre-incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Taiwan investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Company notarization before a Taiwan notary public then TECO authentication then Consular Legalization by the competent PRC embassy or consulate. If the issuing authority is located in an Apostille Convention state, the parallel exclusive path is notarization plus Apostille; no sequential combination of Apostille and Consular Legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum of Association of the Taiwan investing entity (certified extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Company Registration Authority / Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notarial certification of the certified extract then TECO authentication then Consular Legalization by the PRC embassy or consulate. For a Hague Apostille jurisdiction, the alternative exclusive route is notarization plus Apostille; the two routes are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / Creditworthiness Certificate for the Taiwan investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer signature notarized before a Taiwan notary public then TECO authentication then Consular Legalization by the PRC consular authority. For a bank located in a Hague Apostille member state, the exclusive path is notarization plus Apostille; Consular Legalization is not to be chained after an Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner Register Extract and UBO Declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan MOEA UBO filing extract or the PBOC/SAMR Beneficial Owner Information System where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If issued by Taiwan authorities, apply Taiwan notarization then TECO authentication then PRC Consular Legalization. If issued by mainland PRC authorities, no foreign authentication is required for domestic filing. If issued by an Apostille Convention state, apply notarization plus Apostille only; never combine the Apostille and Consular Legalization tracks.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover all legal entity shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, supervisors, senior management, authorized signatories, and general partner personnel against: the OFAC SDN List and all sectoral and derivative sanctions programs; the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs and MOFCOM sanctions lists, including the Unreliable Entity List; Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission sanctions and PEP notices where applicable; domestic PEP databases maintained by PBOC and public security organs; and negative media, insolvency, criminal record, and adverse regulatory action sources. Enhanced due diligence is required for a medium-risk venture capital general partner with capital call wires and Swift transfers. All exact and fuzzy matches must be escalated to the AML compliance officer within 24 hours; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation must be retained for at least five years and refreshed on a risk-sensitive basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and local Administration for Market Regulation enterprise name pre-registration online module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Chinese-language company name is mandatory and must follow a four-tier structure: administrative division, distinctive Chinese-character trade name, industry or business characteristic, and legal form, using Simplified Chinese characters. English and pinyin transliterations are permitted only as ancillary to the registered Chinese name; any phonetic transliteration must correspond exactly to the registered Chinese characters. Inconsistencies between the English ancillary name and the Chinese registered name will result in rejection. For foreign-invested enterprises, the foreign name may appear in the joint venture contract, but the official registered name must be in Simplified Chinese and must comply with the SAMR naming guidelines.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or entrusted agency must obtain the written rejection notice from the local Administration for Market Regulation, identify the statutory basis, and within fifteen working days file an administrative reconsideration petition with the directly superior AMR or the same-level people's government, attaching the corrected name structure, industry classification, and any required ministerial approvals. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit with the competent People's Court within six months of service of the reconsideration decision. During appeal, a parallel new name reservation may be filed using a revised distinctive name that does not duplicate existing registered trade names and does not contain prohibited sensitive tokens. The applicant should preserve evidence of online submission timestamps and SAMR decision records to support any judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are generally not permissible for a venture capital general partner management entity in mainland China. The local Administration for Market Regulation requires a registered address that is a fixed, independently identifiable business premises; the tax authority insists on an actual place of management and business premises for VAT invoice verification, payroll registration, and corporate income tax site inspections; commercial banks uniformly reject virtual office addresses for opening basic deposit accounts and capital call settlement accounts because they cannot perform on-site KYC and anti-fraud due diligence. A lease agreement for at least one year

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, including Articles 7 and 9 on capital verification and defective incorporation, Article 18 on company names and business scope, Article 20 on accounting and financial reporting, Articles 98-113 for a company limited by shares or Articles 128-196 for a company limited by shares, as applicable. Foreign ownership and investment approval are governed by the Foreign Investment Act and its implementing regulations. Regulated securities investment activities may additionally fall under the Securities Investment Trust and Consulting Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan, through the competent local government company-registration office or the One-Stop Online Company Registration platform
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration, accompanied by the Articles of Incorporation, capital verification documents, shareholder and director information, and foreign-investment approval documents where applicable
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Taiwan has no general statutory minimum paid-up capital for an ordinary limited company or company limited by shares. The subscribed capital must be sufficient for the proposed business and must be fully paid before registration. A Taiwan bank account is normally opened for capital remittance, and a certified public accountant issues a capital verification report. Foreign-invested capital must follow the approved investment-remittance procedure; no general statutory escrow account is required after verification.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts and records the subscription by each shareholder for the shares stated in the approved subscription schedule, subject to receipt and verification of the subscribed capital. RESOLVED, that the registered office shall be established at the address approved in the incorporation application, with authority granted to management to execute the lease and registration documents. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Chairperson, [Name] General Manager, and [Name] Company Secretary, each to serve under the Articles of Incorporation and applicable law. RESOLVED, that officers are authorized to complete all filings, banking, tax, foreign-investment, and licensing procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm entity form, name, and regulated business scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs; Financial Supervisory Commission for regulated securities activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a Taiwan limited company or company limited by shares rather than relying on a non-Taiwanese joint-venture label. Conduct company-name and business-scope pre-checks. Define whether the entity will only manage private venture investments or will provide securities investment consulting, discretionary portfolio management, fund administration, or public-fund services. Do not commence regulated activities before obtaining the relevant approval or license.
required_dossiers: Proposed Chinese and English company names
Detailed business-scope descriptions and applicable Taiwan business codes
Shareholding chart and ultimate beneficial ownership information
Foreign-investor corporate registration and authorization documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise the name or business items, remove reserved or regulated wording, and resubmit the pre-check. Obtain a written regulatory classification from the competent authority where the proposed venture-capital management activities are ambiguous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Investment Promotion, Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the foreign-investment application before remitting foreign capital or completing the capital subscription. Provide authenticated corporate documents, ownership information, investment amount, proposed business, source of funds, and appointment documents. Foreign documents should be legalized or otherwise authenticated under applicable Taiwan procedures and translated into Chinese where required.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder certificate of incorporation or equivalent
Ownership and ultimate beneficial ownership chart
Passport or identification documents of responsible persons
Chinese translations and authentication or legalization evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to information requests within the specified period, amend the investment plan or ownership structure, and obtain sectoral clearance if the authority classifies the activity as financial or otherwise restricted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the registered office and prepare incorporation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent local government company-registration office or One-Stop Online Company Registration platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a lease or obtain a registered-office consent. Confirm zoning, building-use, and address eligibility for financial or professional services. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation, shareholder list, director consents, responsible-person consent, and incorporation application. Foreign-language documents must be accompanied by accurate Chinese translations.
required_dossiers: Director and supervisor information, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct address, zoning, translation, signature, or constitutional defects and resubmit the application. Replace an ineligible office address before filing the final registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the preparatory bank account and remit capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan commercial bank approved to handle foreign-exchange and corporate accounts; Central Bank rules apply to foreign-exchange reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a preparatory account in the proposed company name or other bank-approved format. Remit the approved subscription capital through banking channels, identify the remitter consistently with the approved investor, and retain SWIFT and bank remittance records. Do not use cash or undocumented third-party remittances.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct remitter-name discrepancies, obtain bank clarification, return or re-remit nonconforming funds where required, and update the investment authority before using the capital.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Taiwan CPA to verify receipt and availability of subscribed capital. Provide bank statements, remittance evidence, shareholder records, and incorporation documents. Obtain the CPA capital verification report in the form accepted by the registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Reconcile any shortfall or timing mismatch, correct shareholder or remitter records, and obtain a replacement CPA report before registry submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, or the competent local government company-registration office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed company-registration application electronically or in the prescribed physical format with the Articles, CPA report, shareholder and director records, office evidence, foreign-investment approval, and required translations. Pay the applicable registration fee. Notarization is generally not required for every Taiwan document, but foreign corporate documents must satisfy authentication or legalization requirements and powers of attorney must meet filing formalities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer the registry query within the stated deadline, submit corrected documents, cure signature or translation defects, and request reinstatement if the application is rejected or withdrawn under the applicable procedural rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration tax, banking, and foreign-exchange procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance; competent local tax office; commercial bank; Central Bank where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the unified business number and complete tax registration. Convert the preparatory account into the operating account, transfer verified capital, and retain bank evidence. Register electronic invoices if applicable, establish accounting books, and complete foreign-exchange reporting and capital-utilization reporting required by the investment approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax-registration data, reconcile bank and tax records, and file supplemental foreign-exchange or investment-utilization reports where a reporting discrepancy is identified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain conditional financial-sector authorization before operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission, Taiwan; Securities and Futures Bureau, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Map each proposed service against the Securities Investment Trust and Consulting Act and related regulations. If the company provides securities investment consulting, discretionary investment management, securities investment trust, or public-fund services, apply for the relevant enterprise approval or license and satisfy capital, responsible-person, internal-control, compliance, and staffing requirements. Pure proprietary investment or permitted private-fund management may not require a universal standalone license, but the classification must be confirmed before launch.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Narrow the service scope, obtain a written no-objection or classification response, cure capital or personnel deficiencies, and refile the license application without conducting the unlicensed activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs for company and business registration; Financial Supervisory Commission for regulated securities investment or fund-management services; local government authorities for premises and building compliance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing or industrial operating permit applies to a non-industrial venture-capital management office. If the actual services constitute securities investment consulting or discretionary investment management, the applicable title is a Financial Supervisory Commission-approved Securities Investment Consulting Enterprise or other specific approval under the Securities Investment Trust and Consulting Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Taiwan, Environmental Impact Assessment Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally Exempt for an ordinary office-based venture-capital management entity with no manufacturing, construction, significant emissions, wastewater treatment plant, or physical processing operation. A project-specific review is required if the entity develops or operates a facility falling within a prescribed EIA category.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: An office-only entity ordinarily has no industrial wastewater, process VOC, or manufacturing-emission permit. Any wastewater, air emissions, hazardous substances, or waste must comply with the Water Pollution Control Act, Air Pollution Control Act, Waste Disposal Act, Toxic and Concerned Chemical Substances Control Act, and local permit conditions. Industrial discharges require applicable discharge permits and effluent standards; hazardous waste must be segregated, documented, stored, and transferred to licensed contractors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before occupying the premises, confirm building-use compatibility, fire-prevention equipment, evacuation routes, emergency lighting, and occupancy limits with the local fire department and building authority. Structural-load inspection is generally relevant only where the premises are altered, heavily fitted out, or used for unusual loads. An office must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including risk assessment, emergency procedures, workplace facilities, and required employee health and safety measures. No factory registration or industrial workplace clearance is normally required for an ordinary office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Republic of China (Taiwan) - Tax Administration through the National Taxation Bureaus; official electronic portal is the MOF Tax Portal at https://www.tax.nat.gov.tw, with the Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform at https://www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw serving as the statutory e-invoice exchange infrastructure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity or a Taiwan-resident JV with non-resident shareholders, the statutory Tax ID (Unified Business Number) is obtained by completing tax registration at the local National Taxation Bureau after company registration has been certified by the Ministry of Economic Affairs. The procedure is: (1) submit the incorporation documents, the approved articles of association, the foreign investor identification or parent company certificate, the internal revenue registration application, and proof of the domestic business premises; (2) receive the eight-digit Unified Business Number as the combined corporate income tax and VAT file number; (3) where the entity is a non-resident enterprise without a fixed place of business, apply for a non-resident profit-seeking enterprise tax file number with the National Taxation Bureau before making the first Taiwan tax filing or refund claim. No foreign-entity check-the-box or elective classification is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election or any statutory entity-classification election; a JV limited company is always treated as a corporation taxable at the entity level under the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax (Taiwan VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$80,000 average monthly taxable sales; businesses whose average monthly sales exceed NT$80,000 must register as business tax taxpayers. If average monthly sales exceed NT$200,000, the business must issue uniform invoices and is a standard 5% VAT payer. Small businesses between NT$80,000 and NT$200,000 average monthly sales are subject to a special 1% business tax and cannot claim input VAT credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Standard VAT payers in Taiwan must issue and transmit electronic uniform invoices under the mandatory e-invoice scheme. Invoices must be created through an MOF-certified Turnkey transmission software or an approved service provider, and the invoice and recipient identification data must be uploaded to the Ministry of Finance Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform within 48 hours of issuance. The system performs automatic fiscal reconciliation and assigns a random encrypted digital invoice number for anti-fraud verification. Failure to transmit electronically, use of uncertified invoice software, or late transmission can result in disallowance of input VAT deductions and statutory penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Articles 7 and 8 of the Business Tax Act is available where the taxpayer proves actual export of goods from Taiwan customs territory, documented by a valid Customs export declaration, or where Taiwanese services (including qualifying offshore digital services) are provided to nonresident persons, consumed or performed exclusively outside Taiwan, and paid for in foreign currency. The zero-rated sale must be recorded on a zero-rated uniform invoice and matching foreign exchange receipt evidence must be retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export clearance serial number) issued by the Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance
Marine Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical carriage out of Taiwan
Bank-issued Foreign Exchange Proceeds Settlement Certificate or Foreign Currency Receipt Confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: On audit, the National Taxation Bureau will claw back the 5% VAT, assess late interest, and impose a delinquency penalty of up to five times the amount of tax evaded or at least NT$30,000 under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act if the exporter cannot present the Customs export declaration, transport documents, and foreign exchange settlement evidence. Fabrication of banking or customs records can expose the taxpayer to criminal tax evasion liability and related fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: For the specified Taiwan jurisdiction, the competent monetary authority is the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC); the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) supervises financial institutions and relevant financial activities. The payload also identifies China as the sovereign country and describes a Sino-foreign equity joint venture. Those identifiers do not establish that the entity is a Taiwan company or that it may operate in Taiwan. Confirm the place of incorporation, investor nationality, and intended place of business before applying either jurisdiction's rules. Mainland China and Taiwan have separate legal, banking, and foreign-investment regimes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Taiwan dollar (TWD) is not subject to a general requirement to convert all current-account receipts or payments into TWD. Authorized banks process foreign-exchange transactions subject to applicable declaration, documentation, and reporting requirements. Current-account payments, including trade and bona fide service payments, are generally remittable against supporting documents. Capital-account transactions, including foreign investment, capital contributions, loans, securities investments, and repatriation of investment proceeds, may require prior approval, registration, or reporting depending on investor status, transaction type, and applicable sector restrictions. Dividends and liquidation proceeds are not automatically remittable: the company should establish distributable profits, satisfy tax and corporate-law requirements, and provide bank and investment-registration evidence. Mainland Chinese investment into Taiwan is subject to distinct approval and restriction rules and must not be treated as ordinary foreign investment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan generally does not impose a universal statutory deadline to surrender export proceeds or a mandatory conversion ratio requiring exporters to convert foreign-currency receipts into TWD. Receipts remain subject to authorized-bank processing, applicable foreign-exchange declarations and reporting thresholds, and documentary checks. The bank should classify each receipt correctly and retain the export, invoice, contract, and shipping evidence required for the transaction. Confirm current CBC rules and applicable thresholds with the servicing bank before execution; rules differ for mainland China and must be assessed separately if the entity is incorporated or operating there.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a substitute for a locally banked corporate treasury account. Offshore electronic-money institutions are not a substitute for a Taiwan-licensed bank or an authorized foreign-exchange intermediary. Use may be limited by provider eligibility, local licensing, transaction purpose, foreign-exchange controls, and the need to evidence capital contributions and investment proceeds. Obtain bank and counsel confirmation before routing fund subscriptions, capital calls, investment proceeds, or regulated financial-business payments through a fintech provider.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding may be available at a bank's discretion, but is not assured. Banks commonly require authenticated corporate records, beneficial-owner and controller identification, specimen signatures, and enhanced review for a cross-border venture-capital manager. A director's physical appearance is not a universal statutory requirement; a bank may require an in-person interview, local representative, notarization, legalization, or additional verification. Mainland Chinese ownership, a mainland-incorporated applicant, or a Taiwan financial-services activity may trigger additional approvals or prevent onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unresolved mismatch between China as the stated sovereign country, Taiwan as the stated jurisdiction, and the proposed Sino-foreign equity joint-venture form.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the certificate of incorporation and full constitutional documents; identify the actual place of incorporation, registered office, tax residence, and operating locations; provide a group chart and investor-nationality schedule; obtain written advice identifying the applicable mainland China and Taiwan investment-approval regimes. Do not represent a mainland joint venture as a Taiwan entity or assume that approval in one jurisdiction authorizes business in the other.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Venture-capital general-partner activity may constitute regulated securities investment, investment advisory, fund management, or another licensed financial activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the proposed activity and fund-flow memorandum, fund and manager structure chart, draft fund documents, investor eligibility and solicitation plan, portfolio investment policy, fee schedule, and written Taiwan regulatory analysis. Obtain required FSC or other competent-authority approvals before conducting any regulated activity; confirm separately whether activities are permitted under mainland China rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capital, beneficial ownership, investor nationality, or ultimate source of wealth, including funds originating in mainland China.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certified ownership records through natural persons, identity and address evidence, tax-residency information, audited financial statements, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, investor subscription records, capital-call notices, and bank statements tracing funds to the remitting account. Provide required foreign-investment approvals and explain any intermediaries or nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party receipts, unexplained capital-call amounts, or payments inconsistent with the stated venture-capital business purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed fund and subscription documents, capital-call notices, investor register, board approvals, investment or expense agreements, invoices, payment instructions, and a reconciliation linking each remittance to its legal purpose and beneficial payer or payee. Require remitters and beneficiaries to use accounts in their own legal names unless the bank has approved a documented exception.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments involving restricted jurisdictions, sanctioned parties, high-risk counterparties, or complex fund structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide counterparty identity and ownership screening, sanctions and adverse-media results, transaction rationale, underlying contracts, origin and destination bank details, and an escalation record. Screen against applicable Taiwan, mainland China, UN, and relevant correspondent-bank sanctions requirements; obtain bank clearance before processing an alert-sensitive transaction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: First confirm the entity's incorporation jurisdiction, investor nationality, sector eligibility, and required foreign-investment approval or registration. For a Taiwan entity, obtain applicable investment approval before remittance where required, open the appropriate account with an authorized bank, and remit from the investor's own account by SWIFT with accurate beneficiary details and a truthful purpose narrative identifying the equity contribution and investor. Provide the bank with the approval or registration evidence, subscription or joint-venture documents, board resolutions, investor identity and ownership records, and source-of-funds evidence. Ensure the bank records and reports the receipt under the correct capital transaction classification and retain evidence linking the funds to the registered investment. Do not route mainland-origin funds through a third country to evade applicable approval, restriction, or reporting requirements. For a mainland-incorporated entity, apply mainland China capital-account, foreign-investment, and bank procedures instead; Taiwan procedures do not govern that account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use an authorized bank and a transaction-specific payment purpose supported by executed contracts, invoices, delivery or service evidence, and required tax documents. SWIFT MT103 may be used for eligible cross-border payments, subject to correspondent-bank screening and bank documentation. Commercial letters of credit may be used for genuine goods transactions under the agreed documentary-credit terms; they are not a substitute for approvals or evidence required for financial-investment flows. For dividends or investment proceeds, provide audited or otherwise acceptable financial statements, corporate resolutions, tax-clearance or withholding evidence where applicable, and foreign-investment registration or approval records. For fund investments, management fees, and capital returns, obtain bank confirmation of the correct classification and any applicable licensing, approval, or reporting requirements before payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank, subject to bank eligibility, transaction documentation, and a genuine underlying exposure where required.
Non-deliverable forwards where offered by an authorized counterparty and permitted for the relevant currency pair, customer, and documented exposure.
Foreign-exchange swaps and currency swaps with an authorized bank, subject to counterparty approval, exposure and purpose documentation, and applicable reporting requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally 1 May to 31 May following the fiscal year-end; extensions may apply under prescribed conditions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may incur a penalty generally equal to 10% of tax payable, subject to statutory minimum and maximum amounts; non-filing may lead to tax assessment and higher penalties. Taiwan has no general annual franchise renewal or automatic annual strike-off deadline.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders; Ministry of Economic Affairs or competent local company registry only where a registrable change results
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within six months after the end of each fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or document the meeting may result in Company Act penalties, governance invalidity risks, and director liability. Registrable changes must generally be filed within the applicable statutory period, commonly 15 days.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding tax and income information reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by 31 January following the relevant calendar year for annual withholding and income statements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, incomplete, or inaccurate reporting may trigger administrative fines, reassessment, and liability for unpaid withholding tax, interest, and related penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements, where legally required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders and, where applicable, the competent securities or financial regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Complete before the annual shareholders' meeting and within any applicable Financial Supervisory Commission or sector-specific filing deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain or submit a required audit may result in Company Act or sector-specific penalties, regulatory action, director liability, and restrictions on licensed financial or investment activities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Licensed investment-business annual regulatory reporting, if the entity operates as an FSC-regulated investment or securities business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission and applicable industry association
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Deadlines depend on the specific license, including securities investment consulting, discretionary investment management, or securities investment trust activities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate regulatory reporting may result in fines, corrective orders, business restrictions, suspension, or revocation of the relevant license.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent CPA audit is generally required for a company with paid-in capital of at least NTD 30 million, public companies, and entities subject to financial, securities, investment, or other sector-specific regulation. Additional Financial Supervisory Commission criteria may apply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private companies generally use Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standards or Taiwan IFRS-based standards where applicable. Public companies and specified regulated entities generally use Taiwan-adopted IFRS and related Financial Supervisory Commission rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not impose a universal annual UBO confirmation filing on all companies. The company must maintain accurate shareholder, director, and ownership records and update them promptly after transfers or control changes. Regulated investment and financial businesses must conduct risk-based customer and beneficial-owner reviews and retain AML records under applicable rules.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Typically USD 600-2,000 per year, excluding mail handling, accounting, tax, and licensed-business compliance services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Typically USD 2,000-15,000 for a small private company; regulated investment businesses, foreign-invested entities, and fund-management operations may exceed this range.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday; however, a qualifying venture capital management company may benefit from a 12% investment tax credit for investments in start-up/small technology enterprises under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, a 5-year corporate tax exemption on qualifying new-investment profits (subject to Ministry of Finance approval), and deductions for R&D and personnel training. Dividends distributed from retained earnings are not deductible.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form 15) filed electronically through the Ministry of Finance Electronic Tax Filing System (GoTax / TaxRATE)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final return due within 5 months after the close of the fiscal year (calendar-year companies: 31 May). A provisional self-assessed tax payment is required by 30 September of the current year. A CPA-audited extension to 30 June is available for large enterprises.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue: management fees, advisory fees, carried interest allocations and other fund-management service income derived from venture capital funds under administration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If fees are paid by an offshore fund, that income is Taiwan-source if the services are performed in Taiwan. The total amount must be recorded in TWD using the MOF exchange rate; TP documentation must substantiate the arm’s-length basis of the fee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct cost of operating revenue: compensation and direct third-party expenses traceable to fund management activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident sub-managers require a withholding declaration if the services are rendered in Taiwan; costs lacking economic substance or documentary support will be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: SG&A, rent, salaries, insurance, depreciation, and professional fees attributable to the GP entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border service/royalty payments must be at arm's length and subject to a 20% non-resident withholding tax unless treaty-reduced. Allocation of home-office shared costs must be supported by a cost allocation policy.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income: interest income, dividend income from fund holdings, foreign exchange gains, and other incidental gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source dividend and interest income may be offset by an overseas tax credit if supporting documents are attached. Enter the gross amount in TWD and claim credit in the relevant schedule to prevent double taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book-to-tax adjustments: reconciliation of statutory net income to tax-measured net income, including disallowed entertainment expenses, amortisation write-offs under tax rules, and prior-year loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer pricing adjustments on intercompany transactions must be reflected as an upward correction; failure to do so will trigger an automatic assessment and late-payment surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable: 20% statutory rate applied to taxable income, reduced by provisional tax paid, tax withheld at source, foreign tax credits, and investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This line does not include the additional 21% withholding tax imposed on dividend distribution to a non-resident shareholder; that must be separately deducted and remitted by the GIRO paying agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refundable after the application of all credits and prior provisional payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any refund claimed must be wire-transferred to the entity's Taiwan bank account; refunds to foreign parent entities require a Taiwan tax ID and may be subject to overseas remittance screening.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing within 10 days of the due date incurs a 1% surcharge per two-day delay on tax due (maximum 15%); late filing after tax authority notification triggers a 10% penalty on the assessed tax; underpayment caused by misdeclaration is subject to a fine of up to 2x the evaded tax; fraudulent evasion carries imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to NT$60 million.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For a shareholder resident in a treaty partner jurisdiction, the dividend withholding tax may be reduced to the applicable treaty rate (customarily 5%–10% for corporate shareholders with at least 25% holding). The shareholder must submit, through the Taiwan payor, a Form 895 'Application for Tax Exemption/Reduction of Withholding Tax', a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority, a declaration of beneficial ownership, and a power of attorney. The application must be approved by the regional branch of the National Taxation Bureau before the dividend remittance date. For Mainland Chinese shareholders, the Cross-Strait Taxation Agreement is not in force in Taiwan; hence the statutory 21% rate applies unless a specific administrative ruling is obtained.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 20%; treaty reduced to 10%–15% where applicable under an effective DTA (not applicable to PRC residents). Interest: statutory 20%; reduced to 15% for interest paid to a non-resident financial institution recognized by the Ministry of Finance; treaty rate commonly 10% under DTAs.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory where annual related-party transaction amounts exceed NT$100 million (threshold adjusted annually by MOF); Master File and Country-by-Country Report required when the consolidated global revenue of the ultimate parent group exceeds NT$27 billion.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan has no separate Economic Substance Regulations statute, but the Tax Collection Act and Income Tax Act (Articles 43-1, 43-2) embody an economic-substance and substance-over-form standard. The GP entity must demonstrate a fixed place of business in Taiwan, at least two full-time employees, active board and investment-committee meetings in Taiwan, and independent decision-making. fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing artificial invoices, recording false management fees, concealing carried interest income, mischaracterising taxable fund income as non-taxable rebates, or abusing shell entities in tax havens.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of up to 3x the tax evaded; criminal fine of up to NT$60 million and imprisonment up to 5 years under Income Tax Act Article 110 and Tax Collection Act Article 41; late-payment surcharge of 1% per two days up to 15%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign returns known to be false are joint tortfeasors; the court may pierce the veil and order personal civil restitution of the evaded tax plus interest, issue a travel ban under Tax Collection Act Article 24, freeze personal bank accounts, and impose a sentence of imprisonment of 1 to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a virtual GP with no real Taiwan office, no payroll, no investment-committee meetings, nominee directors, and using a BVI affiliate to shift management fee income away from Taiwan.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income is fully reassessed at an arm's-length profit; operating expenses are disallowed; tax benefit credits are reversed; a deemed dividend is assessed to the non-resident parent with 21% WHT; the company registration may be struck off under the Company Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court may pierce the corporate veil under Company Act Article 154, making controlling directors and shareholders personally and jointly liable for the company's unpaid tax debts; directors may face travel bans and an order to liquidate personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / KYC Failure of the Venture Capital GP
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to apply customer due diligence to fund LPs, not filing currency transaction reports for capital-call wires above the threshold, accepting transfers from shell banks or sanctioned entities, and commingling LP capital with GP operating accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the Money Laundering Control Act of NT$500,000 to NT$5,000,000 per violation; mandatory registration suspension or revocation by the Financial Supervisory Commission; criminal liability for intentional non-disclosure carries imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine of NT$10 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML compliance is a personal statutory obligation; directors and the designated compliance officer are subject to personal fines, disqualification from holding positions in financial services, asset freezes, and travel restrictions pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Misappropriation of Investor Capital / Breach of Fiduciary Duty
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Diversion of LP committed capital to personal accounts, charging undisclosed transaction fees, self-dealing with portfolio companies, or making loans to related shell entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil liability for full restitution and disgorgement of profits; under Criminal Code Articles 335 and 342, embezzlement and aggravated breach of trust are punishable by imprisonment of up to 10 years; the FSC may impose a permanent ban on fund management activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are jointly and severally liable to LPs for damages; the court may order personal asset attachments, issue an injunction against leaving the jurisdiction, and upon criminal conviction enforce imprisonment plus a travel ban.
